title: Where You Sit Changes What You Say
subtitle: 数据统计 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）
meta: 主题语境：数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）　|　核心词汇：position　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 position 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: Last term our statistics group asked a small question: does where you sit change how much you say? There were eleven of us and no equipment beyond two borrowed recorders, so we spent the first week deciding how to count anything at all. Our teacher lent us a laptop and a great deal of pessimism.

First we marked the ① position of every desk on a grid, and then we also noted the ② position of the door, the windows and the clock, which few had looked at twice. We sat through fifteen lessons counting who spoke and how often, and the rule was stern: nothing must depend on anybody's opinion. Every position on that grid later had its own average.

The first result looked wrong. Eleven ③ positions in the front row accounted for nearly half of all the answers. We counted again, and the number held. At that stage we were not ④ in a position to explain why, and our teacher refused to ⑤ take a position until we had run the same count in three other classes.

He had once applied for a ⑥ position at the county statistics office and been turned down, which he mentions rather more often than is wise. Our own class finished second in the school project fair, and second is a peculiar ⑦ position from which to feel proud. We even recorded posture: anybody whose ⑧ position slumped towards the desk spoke measurably less, though we could never separate cause from effect.

None of it meant anything until we looked at the school itself. Eleven classes shared one projector, and that simple fact — the school's own ⑨ position — explained more of our data than any theory we had written down. Finally we ⑩ positioned the two recorders at the back of the room, level with nothing at all, and the pattern became obvious immediately: near the clock, people count the minutes; far from it, they answer. Nobody in our group has sat in the same seat since, and every new position now looks like a question rather than a place.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: D. n. 处境；状况（一个机构所处的局面）
F. n. （比赛中的）名次；位次

answers.why: 被 of every desk 修饰并标在网格上，指每张桌子的具体“位置”。
同样指门、窗、钟所处的“位置”，与第 1 题同义复现。
前排的十一个位置，仍是名词“位置”，此处强调空间方位。
in a position to do 意为“有能力／有条件做某事”，此处说当时还无法解释。
take a position 意为“表明立场”，老师在数据充分前拒绝表态。
apply for a position 意为“申请职位”，宾语是县统计局的工作岗位。
班级得了第二名，此处的 position 指“名次、位次”。
recorded posture 与 slumped 呼应，这里的 position 指坐姿、身体姿态。
十一班共用一台投影仪，说的是学校自身的“处境、状况”。
position＋宾语＋地点状语，是动词“放置、安置”，指把录音机放在教室后面。

那时我们还不能解释其中的原因。（in a position to do）

我们把两台录音机安放在教室后面。（position v.）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 position 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: Our statistics group marked the position of every desk, every window and even the clock on a single grid.
We were not in a position to explain the first result, and our teacher refused to take a position either.
Every position on that grid had its own average, and eleven front-row positions produced nearly half the answers.
He once applied for a position at the county statistics office and was turned down.
Our class finished second, which is a peculiar position from which to feel proud.
The school's own position explained most of the data, and once we positioned the recorders at the back the pattern was obvious.
